scores.claim_text: As of January 31, 2024, Rubrik had 255 issued U.S. patents (and non-U.S.), plus 207 U.S. patent applications pending, covering its Zero Trust Data Security / data-security technology.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=503, n_granted=405 (pre-cutoff 'Patented Case'); category_counts data_security=281 vs other=219; titles are backup/snapshot/recovery/immutable-storage/malware-detection
scores.interpretation: Registry strongly corroborates the IP claim. USPTO shows 405 granted patents (assignee 'Rubrik, Inc.'), comfortably consistent with the 255 issued-US-patents claim (the prospectus count is U.S.-only as of a point-in-time; ODP aggregates the full assignee family and later grants of pre-cutoff filings). The portfolio is squarely in the claimed data-security/backup/recovery/ransomware domain (281 of 500 categorized). No Nikola-pattern divergence. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Rubrik's generative-AI assistant 'Ruby' uses Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service in combination with Rubrik's own proprietary software; Rubrik markets a deep Microsoft Azure partnership.
scores.M_value: Microsoft filings: total_hits=0 (signal INFLATION_SUSPECT); edgar_fts cik=MSFT: 0 hits
scores.interpretation: Microsoft's own SEC filings never mention Rubrik. Per Heuristic 5/8 and the SaaS calibration: the claim is an inbound product integration where Rubrik is the BUYER of Azure OpenAI compute (Ruby assistant), not a material counterparty obligation on Microsoft. Microsoft would not separately disclose one of thousands of Azure OpenAI consumers, so absence is NOT a contradiction. The integration claim is registry-invisible -> UNVERIFIABLE (not manufactured as SEVERE). Note: broad EDGAR FTS shows Rubrik is a genuine externally-recognized ecosystem player (157 mentions across competitor/peer filings), so this is plainly not a fabricated entity.

scores.claim_text: Rubrik names major financial institutions Barclays and Citigroup (Citi) as enterprise customers using Rubrik Security Cloud for cyber resilience.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(search_term='Rubrik', no cik) for external counterparty corroboration
scores.M_value: 157 total EDGAR full-text mentions of 'Rubrik' across filers (top: Commvault, Illumina, JFrog, Wayside/Climb, NetApp, Goldman Sachs lending vehicle). These are mostly competitors, channel/reseller, and lenders -- not the named bank customers separately disclosing Rubrik as a vendor.
scores.interpretation: Buyer-side disclosure threshold (Heuristic 5): large banks (Barclays, Citi) do not separately disclose a backup/data-security software vendor in their 10-Ks -- such a relationship is immaterial to a $100B+ bank. Absence of Barclays/Citi-authored mentions is expected and NOT a contradiction. The broad 157-mention footprint corroborates Rubrik's real market presence and ecosystem standing (a positive existence signal) but cannot independently confirm the specific named-customer engagements -> UNVERIFIABLE. (Barclays is also an underwriter in the deal, disclosed transparently.)

scores.claim_text: Rubrik reported more than 6,100 customers and $784.0M Subscription ARR as of Jan 31, 2024 (up 47% YoY), with 133% dollar-based net retention and 1,742 customers >$100K ARR.
scores.M_check: No federal/registry source covers SaaS ARR, customer count, or net-retention metrics (Heuristic 8).
scores.M_value: n/a -- no covering registry. Audited financials in the 424B4 report total revenue $627.9M FY24 and net loss $(354.2)M, which are internally consistent with the ARR scale (ARR > GAAP revenue is normal for a fast-growing subscription book with deferred revenue of ~$300M increase).
scores.interpretation: Customer counts, Subscription ARR, and net-retention rate are SaaS operating metrics with no independent federal registry coverage. Per the crypto/SaaS calibration these are honestly scored UNVERIFIABLE rather than forcing a weak query. The metrics are at least internally coherent with the audited revenue/deferred-revenue figures (no obvious arithmetic inflation), but external confirmation is not available.

scores.claim_text: In August 2023 Rubrik acquired Laminar Technologies (a DSPM platform) for $104.9M fair value ($90.8M cash), to accelerate its cyber-posture / data-security-posture-management offering.
scores.M_value: Bare 'Laminar' query returned 21 granted patents but for 'Laminar Engineering LLC' (titles like 'MODULAR AMMUNITION COUNTER', CPC F41A) -- an UNRELATED defense-engineering firm, NOT the data-security DSPM startup. Name-variant collision (Heuristic 6).
scores.interpretation: The USPTO match is the wrong 'Laminar' (a firearms/ammunition engineering company), so it neither corroborates nor contradicts. Laminar Technologies was an early-stage Israeli/US DSPM startup that likely held few or no granted patents under that exact assignee name pre-cutoff; absence is uninformative. The acquisition itself ($104.9M, $90.8M cash) is a disclosed, audited business combination reflected in the cash-flow statement ($90.3M paid for acquiring Laminar) -- it is internally documented but not independently registry-verifiable. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Rubrik pursues U.S. government certifications including FedRAMP for its data-security solutions in order to sell to government customers.
scores.interpretation: USAspending shows no resolved federal recipient profile or awards for Rubrik. Crucially, the prospectus does NOT claim existing material federal contract revenue -- the FedRAMP language appears in a RISK FACTOR about needing to OBTAIN certification to be able to sell to government in the future (Heuristic 3: planned/forward, not operational). A company pursuing (not yet holding) FedRAMP authorization would correctly show little/no direct federal prime contracting. Absence is therefore expected and NOT a contradiction of any affirmative claim -> UNVERIFIABLE. (Rubrik's federal sales, if any, would also flow through resellers/SIs, further masking direct UEI presence.)
